tests.question: Where do the two rule sets give materially incompatible guidance on the same trigger?

A11Y-1022.scope: web pointer (mouse/touch) targets, a distinct figure from the 44x44pt/48x48dp touch minimum
A11Y-1022.override: a documented exception under WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 target-size criteria

INTERACT-6001.scope: any interactive tap/click target (buttons, icon controls, mobile form inputs, interactive chart elements) web+native
INTERACT-6001.override: a pointer-only/desktop context governed instead by the web-pointer minimum A11Y-1022 (24x24 CSS px); a control whose hit area is legitimately extended beyond the visual glyph to meet the minimum satisfies the rule (check exception, not a rule defeat)

impeccable_pointer.locator: line 50 (accessibility checklist; the file declares a web-only scope at line 5)

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: The audit checklist applies one 44 x 44 px minimum to interactive targets in a web-scoped file, with no separate case for pointer-only input.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: A11Y-1022 sets a 24 x 24 CSS px web-pointer minimum (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8) distinct from the 44 pt / 48 dp touch minimum; INTERACT-6001's override routes pointer-only or desktop contexts to that rule. A 30 px desktop-only pointer target therefore satisfies the corpus and is flagged by the checklist.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

STRUCT-2011.scope: eyebrow (small uppercase wide-tracking) labels above section headlines

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Eyebrow or kicker labels above headings are disallowed unconditionally; the rule is written as a ban with no override.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: STRUCT-2011 (default strength, must_surface) limits eyebrows above section headings under a count ceiling rather than forbidding them. Bounded use versus categorical ban on the same element.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

STRUCT-2006.scope: hero text-element composition and trust/logo-wall placement relative to the hero

table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: STRUCT-2006 (hero composition) tolerates a single hero eyebrow below its composition-count threshold. Hero-scoped instance of REL-STRUCT-0038.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

STRUCT-2015.scope: container/box nesting depth around a single content region
STRUCT-2015.override: a box has a clear, documented purpose

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Nested cards are treated as categorically wrong, with no exception.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: STRUCT-2015 (contextual enforcement) permits nested containers when the box has a clear, documented purpose. Override versus no-override on the same trigger; scope note: the corpus speaks of container/box nesting, the reference of cards (cards are a subset of boxes).
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Body text set light-on-dark is to be compensated in more than one way, one of them a slight increase in letter-spacing.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: TYPO-1011 (avoid, no override) avoids letter-spacing on body text with no stated exception. Direct contradiction for a common scenario; a light-on-dark carve-out in the corpus would resolve it.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

COLOR-4005.scope: neutral and surface color tokens carry appropriate warmth
COLOR-4005.override: the modern-minimal genre permits chroma-free neutral tokens — the monochrome style of brands such as Stripe or ElevenLabs

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Untinted neutral gray is acceptable by default; tinting neutrals is conditional on the brand hue creating cohesion.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: COLOR-4005 (must_surface) requires tinted or warm neutrals by default unless the genre is modern-minimal. Opposite defaults on the same decision: a non-minimal brand whose gray is right passes the reference and is flagged by the corpus unless genre-tagged.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

COLOR-2002.scope: the palette suits premium-consumer briefs (cookware, wellness, artisan, luxury, heritage-craft, DTC home goods)
COLOR-2002.override: the brief names those colors, or the identity is genuinely vintage, artisan, or warm-craft and the specific palette is justified for that brand

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: The hue choice is to follow what the product means and where its visual direction points, rather than a stock association with the product's category.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: COLOR-2002 encodes a brief-genre to palette default (for example premium-consumer leaning warm) with a brief-justified override. Methodological difference: a genre-based default versus meaning-led hue selection; both admit meaning-justified deviation, and the genre default is the point of friction.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

COLOR-4006.scope: the accent color's viewport coverage stays restrained
COLOR-4006.override: the atmospheric genre permits accent-tinted radial blooms over roughly 20% of the canvas, where the bloom is the design

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Accent dosage is to follow the brief and the chosen visual world; fixed-percentage rules are rejected.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: COLOR-4006's override permits accent radial blooms over roughly 20% of the canvas, a fixed band. Friction on the numeric band only; the shared restraint principle agrees.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

COLOR-4007.scope: an abstract background used as hero enrichment
COLOR-4007.condition: the page has an abstract background
COLOR-4007.override: the atmospheric genre permits up to two warm-toned radial blooms over roughly 20–30% of the canvas, fixed-attached and not animating

impeccable_pointer.locator: line 27 and the section headed 'Apply at system scale'

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: Same rejection of fixed-percentage dosage, plus the principle that decoration must relate to hierarchy and the visual world.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: COLOR-4007 (avoid) permits by override up to two warm radial blooms over roughly 20 to 30% of the canvas. Same tension as REL-VISUAL-0027; partially aligned with the decoration-must-relate principle.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

table.impeccable_side_paraphrase: The contrast table allows 3:1 for large text and for controls, icons and focus indicators, and 4.5:1 for body text.
table.design_pack_side_paraphrase: COLOR-1008 (must_surface, no override) sets a 4.5:1 floor for error and success state colors. A conflict only if that floor is read to include non-text indicators; none if it governs text labels. Lowest confidence of the ten; resolves by clarifying COLOR-1008's text-versus-non-text scope.
table.adjudication: none (no winner picked by the study)

tests.question: How do the corpus's 6 runtime controls relate to Impeccable, and how is runtime coverage accounted?

soft_observations: Control-KIND impedance (architecture, not a semantic conflict): DP dials are semantic rule-gating controls; Impeccable's live.md params are user-facing CSS-var tuning knobs + prose ambition. No shared trigger with incompatible guidance.

DIAL-2002 baseline 6 (energetic motion default) vs Impeccable animate.md restraint-by-default: a soft default-posture difference; the dial's gated target rules are non-conflicting (COMPLEMENTARY), so not a POTENTIAL_CONFLICT.

runtime_accounting.statement: 448 rule/synthesized-rule records were mapped and accounted (T02) and 6 runtime controls were evaluated separately (this test); together these correspond to the 454 runtime records of the corpus. The study does not claim an existing single combined 454-row public ledger, and the 88 support records (85 evidence + 3 conflict) are described separately and were not mapped.
